Pittsburgh ranks 30th in the country in opponent-adjusted EPA and 10th in defensive success rate. Meanwhile, Florida State ranks 104th and 102nd in those two metrics. Florida State's best offensive weapon is running the football, but now they have to face a Panthers defense that's fourth in the country in opponent EPA per rush and third in opponent rush success rate. If the Seminoles can't move the ball, it's going to be tough for them to be competitive in a road game against Pittsburgh. I'll lay the points with the home team. Pick: Pittsburgh -3.5 (-108) Illinois vs. UCLA Best Bet UCLA somehow continues to be underrated in the eyes of both football fans and the betting market. The fact that they're rated lower than the two-loss Alabama Crimson Tide is proof of that. The Bruins' defense can carry them a long way this season, ranking fifth in opponent-adjusted EPA per play and second in opponent success rate. Much like Florida State vs. Pittsburgh, this is a game between one of the best defenses in the country and one of the worst. Illinois ranks 131st in defensive success rate, which has hurt them in several games already this season. I'll continue to ride with UCLA in this Big Ten game and bet on them to cover the double-digit spread. Pick: UCLA -10 (-108) Houston vs. Colorado Best Bet Colorado's defense is one-dimensional. They're ninth in the country in opponent EPA per rush, but they're 98th in opponent EPA per pass, meaning when they face a team that relies on an effective run game, the Buffaloes are in a great spot; but then they take on an elite passing attack, they struggle. Unfortunately for them, Houston has one of the best passing games in the country, ranking seventh in EPA per rush and fourth in pass success rate. That, paired with the fact that Colorado has one of the worst offenses in power conference football, leaves Houston in a great spot to cover as road favorites. My Illinois vs. UCLA prediction backs Bret Bielema's battle-tested Illini as a live underdog, with a physical, defense-first script dictating my full college football picks . FOX has live coverage of this contest at 9 p.m. ET on Friday, Nov. 13. TOP PICK Who will win Illinois vs UCLA: Illinois +9.5 Sell high on UCLA and take Illinois at +8.5 or better. The Bruins are 9-0 ATS and are running away with the Big Ten, but that doesn't mean they're a juggernaut. No single result on their resume is something Bret Bielema's squad isn't also capable of pulling off, so these teams are therefore still in a similar tier. UCLA's offense has stalled, ranking 86th in success rate and 133rd in explosiveness since Week 6 . That concern is exacerbated after starting tackle Hall Schmidt and starting center Riley Robell left the Minnesota game with injuries. Illinois has the better offense, checking in at 39th in EPA per play and 33rd in explosiveness over that span, and is therefore an appealing two-score underdog. Illinois vs UCLA Over/Under pick: Under 48.5 In a wet, rainy, short-week game, I'm betting on sloppy offensive results. UCLA's defense has been utter nails, leading the nation in EPA per play since Week 6. Sahir West (7.5 TFLs) is a terror on the edge, and linebacker Sammy Omosigho has played his way into high NFL Draft pick status as the Big Ten's highest-graded defender (92.0) at any position per PFF. Illinois' defense has experienced a revival since coordinator Bobby Hauck was fired. The secondary is a strength, featuring a wealth of experience, and a green front seven has drastically improved since the start of the season. Neither team will push the tempo, leading to a leisurely pace and offenses that rely on sustained drives. The Bruins rank 125th in seconds per snap (29.2), preferring to slowly drain the life out of opponents, and the Illini aren't far ahead at 90th (27.4). Illinois vs UCLA prop: First half Under 23.5 With the weather, Illinois' cross-country travel on a short week, and UCLA's defensive-first philosophy, this contest should start slow. The Bruins are 1-5 O/U against the first-half total in their last six home games, relying on a salty defense that makes life miserable for opposing offenses. The Illini are used to slow starts, averaging 18.4 total points in the first half in their last five games while exceeding 23.5 points just once. Illinois vs UCLA combo It's difficult to create margin in low-scoring games, so an Illinois cover correlates well with a low-scoring game. The Bruins haven't reached 5.7 yards per play or better in four of their last five games. A lack of offensive firepower and a suddenly listless rushing attack will show through. Illinois has been lifeless on the defensive side of the ball in creating takeaways. A poor Havoc ranking is a product of minimal tackles for loss and a pass rush rank at 121st, per PFF . Dieffenbach is coming off a game with just eight completions for more than 300 yards against Minnesota. Action Network's Betting Power Ratings project UCLA to exceed market expectations, power-rated as an 11-point favorite over Illinois. The Fighting Illini have won four straight and hve qualified for a bowl, taking any pressure off must-win games for a postseason appearance. Look for UCLA's Defensive Havoc and Dieffenbach's explosive passing to cover the number against an Illinois team that has lost big in two previous Big Ten West Coast trips. Pick: UCLA -10 or Better

UCLA has found a nice quarterback in Ty Dieffenbach, as starter Nico Iamaleava went down with an injury about a month ago. Dieffenbach has led the Bruins to four convincing wins, and now Illinois is his next challenger. The Illini defense has risen from the dead . Illinois football has a chance to rattle the College Football Playoff cages against UCLA I would imagine not many people are giving Illinois a chance to knock off UCLA on Friday night. This is a matchup between an undefeated Bruins program that is ranked No. 4 in the College Football Playoff, and an Illinois team that just a month ago was looking at limping into a bowl game. Trending ROTHSTEIN 45: Daily college basketball rankings for 2026-27 season Illini Inquirer previews Illinois football's Friday night kickoff at No. 4 UCLA with Bruins to know, Illini in the spotlight, keys to the game and staff score predictions CHAMPAIGN — Like most who appreciate the tradition of the Big Ten and college football at large, Illinois head coach Bret Bielema has great affection for the majesty of the Rose Bowl. Bielema played in the 1991 Rose Bowl as an Iowa defensive lineman, though the Hawkeyes took a 46-34 loss to Washington. Bielema gave his father, Arnie, his Rose Bowl watch he earned from that game, and his father wore that watch until his death last month. Bret Bielema wore that watch all of last week leading into Friday's 24-13 win over Nebraska — on Dad's Day at the university. As a coach, Bielema then led Wisconsin to three straight Rose Bowl Games, coaching them in two (211 and 2012) before leaving the Badgers for Arkansas before the 2013 Rose Bowl Game. Before this trip to Pasadena to play No. 4 UCLA , Bielema made sure to remind his players — or teach them — the history behind the Bruins' home venue. "To have this moment, I'm going to show the guys a video [on Monday] because I'm making a really big deal about playing in the Rose Bowl, how awesome this is," Bielema said. Oh, and this game against a top-five opponent gives the rejuvenated Fighting Illini a chance to really push its midseason turnaround to another tier. Illinois (6-3, 4-2 Big Ten) has won four straight games to clinch a bowl bid, something that seemed unlikely following a 2-3 start and blowing a 16-point second-half lead at Michigan State and losing starting quarterback Katin Houser to a hand injury before pulling out a 38-37 win overtime. Now, Illinois faces one of its toughest tasks of the season against the Bruins (9-0, 6-0 Big Ten), who have gone from bottom of the Big Ten to the conference's top-ranked team under first-year head coach Bob Chesney . But Friday's 8 p.m. CT kickoff (FOX) also gives the Illini a massive opportunity. "These moments, these opportunities don't come about very often," Bielema said. "Obviously to play in the Rose Bowl is a whole huge deal. I kind of made an important point to them all year, but to play a team of this caliber who's undefeated in Game 10 is just absolutely awesome. So I think our guys are excited for the moment." A win at a top-10 team would give Illinois, which beat No. 18 Oregon two weeks ago, the type of win that makes the College Football Playoff committee take them seriously entering the final two weeks of the season. "The opportunity obviously to go play a nationally ranked undefeated team at their home spot, it'l be a tremendous challenge. We're going to have to play extremely well," Illinois offensive coordinator Barry Lunney Jr. said. "But one of the things about fun about college football is the opportunity to make memories and certainly we have that opportunity on Friday." away.headline: Bob Chesney speaks on Ty Dieffenbach after Week 11 win over Illinois
away.source: USA TODAY College Sports Wire on MSN
away.blurb: Bruin QB Ty Dieffenbach left the game injured, missing most of the third quarter, before returning late in the game to close out the victory. Here’s what Chesney had to say about his quarterback after UCLA’s 10th-straight win. The No. 4 UCLA Bruins had to battle in the rain at the Rose Bowl but they ultimately left with a 22-14 win , moving their record to 10-0 on the season . First-year head coach Bob Chesney has revitalized the UCLA football program in less than a year, implementing a mental toughness that was previously absent from the program. UCLA outlasted Illinois , who refused to give up. Illinois QB Katin Houser struggled for much of the game but had a chance to tie the game late in the fourth quarter before the Bruin defense got one final stop to end the game. “He did a great job. At halftime, his shoes are off, no shoulder pads on. I’m like ‘Gotta get your shoes back on’ but we had to make sure that everything was good in there and he was ready to go,” Chesney said . “To go back in there, and to lead the team down the field and score after having to put yourself back in the locker room and in the tent, there’s a lot he had to go through there. He’s a warrior. It’s what he’s growing and becoming, it’s what I’m really excited about.” Dieffenbach earned the Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week last week versus Minnesota, he followed it up with a 13-20 through the air for 232 yards and two touchdowns with an interception. away.blurb: The Fox Sports broadcast later reported Dieffenbach had sustained an upper body injury and was questionable to return. He re-entered the game later in the third quarter, with the Bruins up 12-7. A three-star recruit out of Agoura Hills, California, Dieffenbach began his college career at Pittsburgh but didn't see any game action in his first two seasons. He started 12 games for Cal Poly last year, posting 1,305 passing yards, a 56.8% completion rate, 9 touchdowns and 9 interceptions. UCLA has already weathered one major quarterback injury. Fortunately, it appears to have avoided another in a close Big Ten victory. Ty Dieffenbach, a bright spot for the No. 4-ranked Bruins since starter Nico Iamaleava's knee injury , exited Friday's 22-14 victory against Illinois with an apparent injury. Third-string quarterback Madden Iamaleava, Nico's brother, replaced him under center with UCLA up 10-0. The injury occurred less than a minute before halftime, when Dieffenbach took a hard hit from Illinois defensive lineman Carter Janki on an incomplete pass. Dieffenbach was writhing on the ground while holding his left shoulder, then had to be helped off the field and into the blue tent. He moved to the locker room at halftime, with a clear limp. There was no sign of him at the start of the third quarter, with Iamaleava continuing to lead the UCLA offense. He threw a 26-yard touchdown pass to Semaj Morgan early in the fourth quarter to put UCLA ahead 19-7. Dieffenbach finished 13-for-20 for 232 yards, 2 touchdowns and 1 interception. Dieffenbach transferred to UCLA from Cal Poly last offseason and sat second on the QB depth chart until the elder Iamaleava went down in Week 6 against Oregon. Since then, the Bruins' offense has barely missed a beat with Dieffenbach reeling off four straight wins in his first four starts before this week. UCLAv(10-0) is in the thick of the College Football Playoff race and is one of two remaining undefeated teams in the FBS, alongside No. 2 Utah.

Ford Stadium — Dallas, TX Spread: SMU (-1.5) Over/under: 61.5 All-time series: SMU leads, 3-1 Last meeting: Wake Forest 13, SMU 12 — October 25, 2025 Current streak: Wake Forest, 1 (2025) Setting the scene This might be the ACC regular season game of the year. For the first time in College Football Playoff history, the ACC champion is guaranteed an automatic bid. Thus, just getting access to Charlotte keeps the door ajar for Wake Forest and SMU in this high-stakes conference showdown. The Demon Deacons are one of the hottest teams in college football, winning six consecutive games, primarily in blowout fashion. But the Mustangs haven’t ever lost an matchup at Gerald J. Ford Stadium, faring 12-0 in their previous contests. A Wake Forest win propels the Demon Deacons to the doorstep of the ACC Championship Game. An SMU win creates chaos, bringing a cluster of 2-loss teams back into championship consideration, including itself. The ACC races greatly hinges on what unfolds Saturday afternoon on The Hilltop. Wake Forest Demon Deacons outlook Wake Forest (8-1, 5-1 ACC) is ranked No. 13 by the College Football Playoff committee, situated as the second-highest ACC team. Since its lone September loss to Miami (FL), the Demon Deacons have been as dominant as anyone in the FBS. During the last five games of its six-game win streak, Wake Forest has defeated opponents by an aggregate score of 264-31, or an average of 53-6 per game. The Demon Deacons used a dominant defense to stun SMU 13-12 in last year’s meeting in Winston-Salem, but this season, the offense has hit its stride under second-year coordinator Rob Ezell. Wake Forest ranks fourth nationally in scoring (43.3 points per game), ninth in total offense, and 10th in passing. Starting quarterback Gio Lopez missed last week’s game against FCS Merrimack with a lower body injury, but the absence was permissible due to the level of opponent. The former South Alabama and North Carolina gunslinger has been phenomenal in his new home, delivering 18 touchdowns against one interception this year, ranking 13th nationally in passing average. His mobility has made defenses pay too, accumulating 317 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season. Lopez’s top target Carlos Hernandez is receiving national recognition. The senior is sixth in the FBS with an average of 105 receiving yards per game, and he regularly strikes from distance. Hernandez has multiple 70-yard touchdowns this season, and he has four outings with at least 110 yards and an end zone appearance. Jack Foley, Kam Shanks, and Antonio Meeks have provided support in this dynamic aerial attack, and the diversity in options allows Wake Forest to have the nation’s ninth-most efficient third down offense. The run game has been serviceable, ranking 43rd nationally in yards per game, while producing 4.94 yards per carry. Ty Clark and Deuce Lawrence have split carries throughout the season, totaling 416 and 327 rushing yards, respectively. Wake Forest’s offensive improvement has somewhat obscured the consistent impact of its defense. The Demon Deacons have only surrendered multiple scores once in their past five games, and they’ve finished 22 consecutive quarters without allowing more than seven points. The result is the country’s 13th-ranked scoring defense and 24th-ranked total defense — a unit which is particularly stingent against the run, surrendering just 85 yards per game on a 2.69 average. Defensive end Langston Hardy is the leader of the run-stuffing effort. He leads all ACC players with 13.5 tackles for loss, while also producing 44 tackles and 5.5 sacks. Backfield pressure has been a signature of this Wake Forest defense, and two other defensive linemen — Gabe Kirschke and Zach Lohavichan — have at least 7.5 tackles for loss. Wake Forest’s defense found the sustainable method of success, and that’s getting stops. The Demon Deacons are fifth nationally in both red zone defense and fourth down defense, finding ways to get off the field in critical situations. The unit can become even more dangerous if it dabbles in the turnover game. Wake Forest has forced just seven takeaways all season, which is tied for the eighth-fewest in the FBS. SMU Mustangs outlook SMU (7-2, 5-2 ACC) prepares for a revenge game against Wake Forest. Had the Mustangs prevailed last October in Winston-Salem, they would have competed in the ACC Championship Game with a College Football Playoff spot on the line. Instead, they fell in a 13-12 heartbreaker on a last-second field goal — one of the program’s four ACC losses since joining the conference in 2024. Zero of those losses transpired at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. SMU has been a different beast at home, and that was evident in its most complete game of the season last Friday against Virginia Tech. Counting games against FBS opponents, the Mustangs registered a season-high 23 first half points, utilizing its strongest start of the season to push past the Hokies, 51-28. The concept of senior day might have lost some luster in the transfer portal era, but Saturday will feature one of the most emotional senior day moments in recent memory. Kevin Jennings is in his fifth year with the program and third as the starting quarterback, and the Dallas area native has poured a lot into the program. Jennings guided the Mustangs to an American Conference title, an ACC Championship Game appearance, a College Football Playoff berth, and a Holiday Bowl victory. Now he’ll play his final game in Dallas, entering the pivotal matchup fifth nationally with 2,764 passing yards and fourth with 25 touchdown passes. The most remarkable part of Jennings’ eye-popping stats is his efficiency. For a quarterback that slings it deep quite often, the senior boasts a 73.9 completion rate, which is second among all players with at least 100 attempts. Jennings has also limited interceptions this year, finishing four of his last five starts without one. SMU’s high-powered passing attack involves a slew of receivers. Yamir Knight, coming off a 103-yard, 3-touchdown performance, is the most frequented with a team-high 50 catches. But Yannick Smith, Jalen Cooper, and Jalen Hale are also heavily involved — especially on downfield attempts — and all three average over 15.0 yards per reception this season. Tight ends Randy Pittman Jr. and Theo Melin Öhrström are also regular targets, tied for second on the team with four touchdown receptions apiece. The Mustangs’ run game is statistically a middle-of-the-road unit, ranked 70th in yards per game and 66th in rushing average. Kendrick Raphael operates as the top option, and he’s scored in seven of nine contests this year. Freshman Christian Rhodes has seen an increasing number of reps since mid-October, and he’s coming off a career-high 92 rushing yards against Virginia Tech. On defense, SMU displays a similar identity to the previous Mustang defenses of the Rhett Lashlee era: defensive line dominance. The Mustangs are one of 17 programs racking up at least 3.0 sacks per game, and defensive end Marques White is the ringleader of the movement. The eighth-year senior notched his third multi-sack game of the season last week, contributing to the turnover battle with a forced fumble and fumble recovery on the same play. But unlike the previous two seasons, SMU isn’t collecting turnovers on a consistent basis. The Mustangs have forced just eight turnovers all year, recovering five fumbles and picking off two passes. Despite the lack of takeaways, the secondary has shown considerable improvement from 2025, skyrocketing from 135th to 42nd in passing yards allowed per game, with safeties Jimmy Wyrick and Sael Reyes playing significant roles in that progress. Last year’s matchup between SMU and Wake Forest was the ultimate defensive battle. Just two touchdowns were scored — one on a 14-play drive and another capping a 41-yard series. There were eight combined turnovers in the matchup, which was decided on Connor Calvert’s 50-yard field goal as time expired. This year’s rematch looks bound to lean more on the higher-scoring end. Wake Forest brings significantly more offensive firepower in this matchup, headlined by the strong connection between Gio Lopez and Carlos Hernandez. The Demon Deacons’ offense has been virtually unstoppable since the start of October, and while SMU should provide some resistance with a formidable defensive line, Wake Forest will still get its points in Dallas. However, SMU can thrive in a shootout style game. The Mustangs are one of the most explosive offenses in the country, ranking ninth in the FBS with 15 plays spanning 40 yards. Wake Forest has excelled at preventing the big play this year, but the Mustangs’ receiving corps should present challenges on the back end that the Demon Deacons haven’t seen since the Miami (FL) loss. This back-and-forth thriller will come down to crunch time. With the backing of its home crowd, SMU improves to 13-0 in ACC matchups at Gerald J. Ford Stadium — a result which will add significant chaos to the final two weeks of ACC play. picks.headline: Wake Forest vs. SMU: Week 11 Betting Odds, Prediction
picks.blurb: Wake Forest enters the game with an 8-1 record, while SMU is 7-2. The game has significant implications for the ACC championship race. Betting odds slightly favor SMU, but the prediction favors Wake Forest in a high-scoring game. Week 11 of the College Football season gets us closer to the precipice of championship weekend. The ACC has a great slate to end the season, and Week 11 features a ton of awesome games. The showstopper is on at Noon ET, with the Wake Forest Demon Deacons taking on the SMU Mustangs. Wake Forest (8-1) has looked the part of a championship contender. There aren't a ton of takeaways from their 76-0 win against Merrimack out of the Football Championship Subdivision (FCS), but it continues a trend of dominance for them. The Demon Deacons. They haven't been within one score of a team since their upset win against Louisville earlier in the season, winning by 20+ in all of the past five matchups and 40+ in three of their past five matchups. SMU (7-2) should be closer to the ACC championship than they are. They proved it with a dominating 51-28 win against then 6-2 Virginia Tech, where their offense scored on nine of their 11 possessions. However, they dropped an easy game against Syracuse on Halloween. They lost 30-27, giving up a last-minute touchdown drive. That's been the only holdup preventing them from being in Wake Forest's spot. If you are looking for some betting advice for the matchup, we've got you covered. Here are the latest odds for the game, courtesy of BetMGM. Wake Forest vs. SMU game odds All college football odds via BetMGM Money Line: SMU -115, Wake Forest -105 Over/Under: Over 60.5 (-110), Under 60.5 (-110) Spread: SMU -1.5 (-105), Wake Forest +1.5 (-115) Wake Forest vs. SMU prediction, pick This might be the matchup with the most stakes in the ACC championship picture. If Wake Forest wins, they'll be 6-1 in the ACC and have tiebreakers over SMU and Louisville in the race, but if SMU wins, they'll be 6-2 in the ACC with one more game against Stanford remaining. If anyone's expecting the 13-12 defensive bout we got last year, throw that out the window. This should be a shootout. Both teams possess some of the best quarterbacks in the nation, with Gio Lopez and Kevin Jennings combining for 4,940 yards, 43 touchdowns, and seven interceptions. They're the biggest reason why either team is at the place it is now. Wake Forest has a few advantages, though. The Demon Deacons are one of the top teams in the nation at stopping the run, allowing just 82.9 yards per game (No. 5 in the country). The Mustangs are slightly above average against the run (133.9 yards per game, No. 45). The Demon Deacons are also favorites in the turnover battle. They're one of the most turnover-averse teams in the country (0.4 giveaways per game, No. 2 in the country), while the Mustangs are pretty turnover-prone (1.5 giveaways per game, No. 95). This game should have no problem hitting the over, with both of these teams boasting some of the top passing offenses in the league. However, give me the Demon Deacons in a road win. With bowl eligibility still in question, Mike Elko's squad will welcome one of the nation's top-ranked teams to Kyle Field for its annual Operation: Blackout game. Texas A&M enters the matchup looking to build momentum after an inconsistent season that has featured significant offensive struggles. Despite sitting at 4-5, the Aggies have shown flashes of defensive promise, allowing 20 points or fewer in five games this season. Meanwhile, Tennessee arrives in College Station following a dominant victory over Kentucky. The Volunteers have one of the nation's most dangerous pass defenses, leading the FBS with 39 sacks. Tennessee vs. Texas A&M Pick: Tennessee -2.5 (-115, Play to -3) My Texas A&M vs. Tennessee best bet is on the Volunteers to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and be sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Tennessee vs Texas A&M Odds, Betting Line, Over/Under Tennessee vs Texas A&M point spread : Tennessee -1.5 (-105), Texas A&M +1.5 (-115) Tennessee vs Texas A&M over/under : 43.5 Total Points (-115o / -105u) Tennessee vs Texas A&M moneyline : Tennessee ML -113, Texas A&M ML -108 Tennessee Volunteers With only a handful of games left in the regular season, Tennessee is firmly in the mix for the playoffs, slotting in at No. 8 in the latest CFP rankings. At 7-2, the Volunteers must avoid dropping a game if they want to keep their hopes of competing for the title alive or risk stumbling out of the playoff picture with plenty of viable contenders hovering beneath them. If Tennessee wants to remain unscathed, then George MacIntyre must do a better job of taking care of the ball while leading an offense that ranks 75th nationally in Havoc allowed. By making it easier for the opposing defense to create disruptions, the Vols are vulnerable to stalling out and giving their opponents generous field position. Fortunately for Tennessee, DeSean Bishop has thrived, averaging nearly 120 rushing yards per game while rattling off 5.4 yards per carry. When Bishop can hit the ground running, the Vols can lean on their star running back, reducing the chance of MacIntyre creating a Turnover-Worthy Play. While the offense has struggled to get into a groove, the defense has been phenomenal, ranking in the top 15 nationally in Explosiveness allowed, Defensive Finishing Drives and Havoc. On the rare occasions when opponents get inside the 20, points come at a premium, with Tennessee allwoing just 2.56 Points per Opportunity. With Tyree Weathersby out with a season-ending injury, negative regression may be looming large over Tennessee's defense if Jordan Norman and Mariyon Dye are unable to make up for his lost production. That puts more pressure on MacIntyre's shoulders to keep the team afloat, a tall task for the inconsistent quarterback. Texas A&M Aggies Since the start of the regular season, Texas A&M has severely underwhelmed, limping into Week 11 at 4-5 after a disheartening loss to South Carolina . Not only were the Aggies unable to take advantage of LaNorris Sellers ' injury, but Marcel Reed also continued to struggle to connect with his pass catchers, completing just 58% of his passes. Reed's inconsistencies have been a thorn in Texas A&M's side this season, drastically lowering the team's ceiling on a weekly basis. With Reed under center, the Aggies have been league-average at best on offense, ranking 64th nationally in Success Rate, 57th in Finishing Drives and 52nd in Havoc allowed. To make matters worse for Texas A&M, Mario Craver , the team's current leader in receptions, is dealing with an injury. While Craver was able to suit up last week, he is noticeably playing at less than 100%, making it easier for opposing defenses to shade their coverage elsewhere without sacrificing too much ground. On the other side of the ball, the Aggies have been much better on defense, ranking well above the national average in Success Rate allowed and Points per Opportunity allowed. While Texas A&M is able to neutralize the middle of the field, the back end has been vulnerable to giving up explosive plays while creating disruptions at a low rate, potentially giving MacIntyre the edge he needs to reduce the amount of Havoc on his throws. Even with Tennessee's pass rush expected to take a hit, it's hard to see Reed capitalizing on Weathersby's injury. The Vols' secondary has excelled in coverage this season, fielding a group that ranks third in Pass PPA allowed and second in Explosiveness allowed. With Reed struggling to pick apart the gaps on the back end, Tennessee can shade its linebackers toward the middle of the field, helping them stuff the run at a higher rate. With more bodies crashing down to the line of scrimmage, Rueben Owens II and KJ Edwards will be forced to fight off contact in the backfield, making it difficult to burst through the trenches. To help pull away on the scoreboard, MacIntyre will have a great opportunity to avoid turnovers while methodically moving the ball against a defense that struggles to create Havoc, improving the quality of his passes. With fewer bodies near the point of contact, the Vols should be able to generate explosive plays at a higher rate, leading to an uptick in their total number of scoring opportunities. With clear advantages on both sides of the ball, place a wager on Tennessee to cover at -3 or better. To diversify your risk, place a separate wager on the Vols to clear the over of 22.5 on the team total. Pick: Tennessee -2.5 (-115, Play to -3)

away.headline: Indiana faces several key injury concerns heading into crucial USC showdown
away.source: Hoosier State of Mind on MSN
away.blurb: Heading into Week 11 against USC, Indiana has several big names that are currently listed on the Big Ten availability report . Most notably, Turbo Richard, Kellan Wyatt, and Joe Brunner have already been ruled out. With Richard out, Lee Beebe Jr. figures to take on a leading role in the Hoosier backfield once again. Beebe stepped up in a big way when Richard was down with injury, and has been a reliable threat on the ground. In total, Beebe has 715 rushing yards to go along with 4 touchdowns on 134 attempts. Veteran OL Joe Brunner is also out. Brunner is a seasoned offensive lineman in his fifth season of college football, and has played a vital role on the Hoosier offensive line this season. He has started all nine games at right guard, and this is the first time he has popped up on the injury report. In his absence, freshman Sam Simpson could see more playing time, unless Cignetti switches things up and moves some names around. LB Rolijah Hardy is listed as questionable, and not having him on the field would be a tough loss for the Hoosiers against a dangerous USC offensive attack. Hardy is second on the team with 58 tackles this season. CB A.J. Harris is listed as probable. Harris has already missed time this season, and has appeared on the injury report several times. USC has a solid passing offense, so getting Harris in the mix would bode well for Indiana's chances of victory. After enjoying a much-needed bye week, the Indiana Hoosiers are set to take the field again in Week 11. Indiana hosts USC on Saturday afternoon in Bloomington in a game that could heavily impact the Big Ten race and College Football Playoff picture. The 4th-ranked Hoosiers find themselves as 8.5-point favorites over the 18th-ranked Trojans, but as we've seen before this season, Indiana has a habit of playing in close games. Looking for a decisive victory on its home turf, Indiana could be without some key playmakers. For the most part, the Hoosiers have stayed healthy this season. Curt Cignetti has an effective strategy in place to keep his team healthy, which includes managing practice workloads, prioritizing player recovery, and emphasizing proper nutrition and conditioning to minimize the risk of injuries. But no matter how effective that plan is, we are still talking about football here. Unfortunately, injuries are a regular sight. The No. 9 Hoosiers (8-1, 5-1 Big Ten) do have some other injury concerns going into a must-win game against the No. 18 Trojans (7-2, 4-2). They four key contributors (three starters) on the report with leading rusher Turbo Richard and defensive end Kellan Wyatt already listed as out for Saturday's game. Jaylen Bell, who stepped in for Harris earlier this season, would likely get the start if the Penn State transfer is ruled out. Skip to main content SI.COM MORE SPORTS NEWS SI.COM WOLVERINES FB SI.COM WOLVERINES BB FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Michigan needs one more win to gain bowl eligibility and the Wolverines will look to make magic happen this weekend in Eugene. The Wolverines made a major change heading into the game, firing Jason Beck, and Kyle Whittingham promoted Jim Harding as the interim offensive coordinator. But we wouldn't expect many drastic changes this late in the season. Tommy Carr is expected to start again this week, but reports have indicated that Bryce Underwood could also see some snaps . If Michigan has any chance to win this game, the Wolverines' offense has to come alive and establish the run . Here's how Michigan on SI sees the game going. Michigan still has one of the best defenses in the country and last week was a major disappointment by their standards — and they didn't even allow a touchdown. But five field goals were too much with how poorly the Wolverines' offense has played. Firing Jason Beck was the right move, but it was too late in the season. Michigan isn't going to have wholesale changes and I just don't see a way for the Wolverines to score enough points to win a game like this on the road. The Wolverines' defense will play tough, but Oregon finds a way to break away in the second half. Firing Jason Beck was the correct move, but that doesn’t mean it is going to fix all or any issues on the offensive side of the ball. Kyle Whittingham and Dan Lanning took shots at each other this week via the media, so I have a feeling this game will be a little extra chippy. Hirschhorn While Michigan stumbles toward its first losing season with a non-truncated schedule since the Brady Hoke era, Oregon has fought its way out of the darkness to at least keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive. The Ducks responded to losses against Oklahoma State, UCLA, and Illinois with wins, and did so mostly without starting quarterback Dante Moore. Conversely, the Wolverines have let bad games snowball and have notched a single multi-score victory all year (Week 3 versus UTEP, a team that currently has a 1-8 record). Michigan still has one of the nation's best defenses at its disposal, but the sheer volume of errors in the other phases has negated that advantage in too many weeks to ignore. The Ducks might not have a unit as dominant as that defense, but they don't have a weakness as obviously exploitable as the Wolverines' offense or special teams. Oregon also doesn't have to overcome a head coach with a penchant for creating roadblocks for his own team . Dan Lanning says he respects Michigan's Kyle Whittingham, but the final score of Saturday's game will probably undercut that claim. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Michigan vs Oregon Odds, Betting Line, Total Michigan vs Oregon point spread : Oregon -10.5 (+100), Michigan +10.5 (-120) Michigan vs Oregon over/under : 39.5 (-110o / -110u) Michigan vs Oregon moneyline : Michigan +310, Oregon -385 Michigan Wolverines To be honest, I'm still a little flabbergasted by how bad it's been in Ann Arbor. To see Kyle Whittingham, who had an esteemed career in Utah for 20 years, go out like this is upsetting. I just don't see how he stays on after this season. It's been madness. And seeing how he fired a guy he brought with him from Utah, offensive coordinator Jason Beck, midseason, it just feels like there's no order here. Because Beck is now gone, offensive line coach Jim Harding is taking over. The problem is, Harding hasn't called plays before, and Whittingham acknowledged that he's not going to be involved. So, would it have been better to just stick with Beck? Too late now. To Whittingham's defense, his offense had all the talent in the world, but zero execution. Quarterback Bryce Underwood was such a disaster that the Wolverines had to turn to Tommy Carr. Wide receiver JJ Buchanan is the only player worth anything, while running backs Savion Hiter and Jordan Marshall average under four yards per carry. So, would you be surprised, after telling you all that, that Michigan ranks 128th in standard down Success Rate and 109th in Havoc allowed? Of course you're not. Luckily for the Wolverines, the defense has been this team's saving grace. Defense has always been Whittingham's forte, so Michigan ranking 12th in the FBS, allowing an average of 16.2 points per game, is par for the course. The Wolverines have managed to stifle both the run and the pass, ranking in the top 10 in Success Rate allowed. Michigan followed in Oregon's footsteps because the Ducks fired their offensive coordinator, Drew Mehringer, a few weeks ago. The Ducks, who had National Championship aspirations this season, sank early on and lost their quarterback, Dante Moore , who suffered a concussion but is now saving himself for the NFL Draft. So, it's been Dylan Raiola taking over under center. Since Oregon fired Mehringer, assistant quarterbacks coach Jay Johnson has been calling plays, and his connection with Raiola has been palpable. Raiola's first action after Moore went so bad that third-string Brock Thomas started against Nebraska , but he ended up bouncing back. Raiola's main target has been Dakorien Moore, who's been generating a ton of volume, including a two- touchdown game with over 120 yards two weeks ago against Northwestern . We've also seen a major uptick in the run game. Jordon Davison is likely going to miss this game after hurting himself last week, but Dierre Hill Jr. has picked up the slack. Hill rushed 13 times for 75 yards and a pair of touchdowns, including a 48-yard house call. Despite all the flaws this team has, the defense has largely been a success. Chris Hampton seemingly has a solid grip on this unit. This is still one of the best pass rushes in college football, led by Matayo Uiagalelei, Teitum Tuioti, Bear Alexander and A'Mauri Washington. This is going to be an interesting duel. Oregon's offense has had a boost since the Mehringer firing, but I can absolutely see Michigan's defense control the pace of this game. Don't worry about the Wolverines' offense; this won't be much of a fight on that end. I mentioned earlier that Michigan is one of the worst teams in Havoc allowed. Well, Michigan's offensive line has been absolutely brutal, allowing 2.1 sacks per game, so I can absolutely see Oregon's defense feasting on Carr, or stuffing Hiter and Marshall. This total is rightfully low at 38.5, and I tend to avoid going under when the total is lower than 40. But let's look at the numbers here. In Michigan's nine games played, it has gone under 38.5 five separate times, and that's not including twice when it went to 39. Because Oregon's offense is potent, the Ducks have only gone under 38.5 on two separate occasions, but one of those games came against UCLA , whose defense has been elite all season. The other went against Illinois, who oddly has been a sieve defensively. I like this game to go under. Pick: Under 38.5 (-110)

At 5-4 and coming off an embarrassing 15-6 loss to Michigan State, Michigan desperately needs something positive. Unfortunately, that opportunity comes against No. 18 Oregon inside Autzen Stadium, one of the loudest and most intimidating venues in college football. The Ducks will have the benefit of a hostile home crowd, while Michigan will be breaking in a new offensive coordinator and attempting to find some semblance of consistency on that side of the ball. It's hardly an ideal combination. When Michigan Has The Ball All eyes will be on interim offensive coordinator Jim Harding , who takes over following Kyle Whittingham's decision to fire Jason Beck. Michigan enters the matchup ranked No. 126 nationally in scoring offense, No. 109 in rushing offense, No. 125 in passing offense and No. 132 in total offense. Those numbers are remarkably poor for a program with Michigan's resources and expectations. Whittingham hasn't officially named freshman Tommy Carr the starter, but all signs point to No. 14 manning the offense. Carr has shown flashes since replacing Bryce Underwood, but he's also operating behind an offensive line that has struggled throughout the season. Against Oregon, those protection issues could become even more glaring. The Wolverines need Jordan Marshall and Savion Hiter to establish something on the ground, particularly early. Otherwise, Carr could find himself facing obvious passing situations against an aggressive defense with the Autzen crowd making communication difficult. Harding doesn't need to reinvent the offense overnight. He needs to simplify things, establish manageable situations and give Carr opportunities to succeed. When Oregon Has The Ball Michigan's defense has been the more reliable unit by a mile, and that group will need another outstanding performance to keep this competitive. Defensive coordinator Jay Hill has enough talent to make things difficult, particularly with players like John Henry Daley, Zeke Berry, Chris Bracy and Jyaire Hill capable of creating disruptive plays. But Oregon presents a different challenge. The Ducks can put considerable pressure on a defense through tempo, athleticism, pure speed and offensive versatility. Michigan cannot afford repeated three-and-outs that force its defense to spend the afternoon on the field. If Oregon establishes an early lead, the Wolverines could find themselves in serious trouble. Michigan's defense should compete, but expecting Harding to completely transform one of America's worst offenses in less than a week is unrealistic. Autzen Stadium only makes matters worse. The Wolverines keep things respectable early before Oregon pulls away, leaving Michigan with two remaining opportunities to secure bowl eligibility. Oregon 27, Michigan 10

One player who is set to see an uptick in snaps is the dynamic Nasir Wyatt, though he is listed as probable as of Thursday evening so he may be banged up. Raiola has emerged from that low point and put together two excellent games in a row, seeking to keep the rhythm going on Saturday and continue to prove himself as Oregon's signal-caller for the long term. Michigan, however, is just hoping to have a somewhat effective game from one of its two struggling quarterbacks. picks.blurb: Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Predictions: Why our Staff is Split on the Winner Skip to main content SI.COM FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS BASKETBALL NEWS Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3) is back on the road this weekend, where it will meet the Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3) in Norman for a game that each side could really use in the win column. For Oklahoma, it won’t mean much in terms of a playoff push, but it will go a long way in salvaging what’s been a lost season. The Sooners don’t have consecutive wins (or losses) on the season yet, but they have collected wins over Texas and Florida in the last five weeks. For Ole Miss, its CFP hopes are on thin ice and to even be somewhat involved in the conversation next month, the Rebels badly need to win their final three regular season games. Ole Miss initially opened as a 2.5-point road favorite last week, but will now enter the weekend as a narrow 1.5-point underdog. Ahead of the Rebels' latest conference matchup, Ole Miss On SI predicts which team wins and why. Ole Miss desperately needs to bounce back in both departments, as it surrendered five sacks and ran for just 66 rushing yards in its loss last week. While there’s no doubt Ole Miss’ offensive line will get tested, and that Oklahoma will be sending consistent pressure, I’m picking Trinidad Chambliss to capitalize on what is looking like his final test against a great collegiate defense. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Ole Miss' Trip to Oklahoma
picks.source: Ole Miss Rebels On SI on MSN
picks.blurb: No team should be judged by how they perform when everything is going its way, just as this Ole Miss program should be judged on how it can respond after the tumult it faced last time out against Georgia. With the Rebels' playoff hopes dwindling to the lowest they have been all season, Pete Golding's squad will need to respond in a big way this afternoon in Norman . Facing an Oklahoma team with a retooled offensive scheme and rejuvenated belief in itself, Ole Miss will need to capitalize on the trend that the Sooners have yet to win consecutive games this season. Just about everything went wrong at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium last weekend for the Rebels, and it's true; everyone has a plan until they get punched in the face. Golding's side took a clean hit to the jaw from the Bulldogs, and Ole Miss will need to claw itself up against Oklahoma if it wants a chance at getting back to the playoffs this season. Trinidad Chambliss Plays a Clean Game Following His Worst Showing Numbers talk, and for Trinidad Chambliss, they're quite damning. Throwing nine passes to the wrong side this season, the Rebels' former Heisman frontrunner is third in the Football Bowl Subdivision for interceptions this year. If Ole Miss wants to win on the road tomorrow and show that it can play in tough road environments, Chambliss will need to clean the turnovers up. The differences between Georgia and Oklahoma are clear, and I truly believe that Chambliss will return to the form he got fans used to in the 2025 season. The Rebels need their star to play a professional game today, and that all starts with taking care of the ball and making the right decisions when the Sooner pass rush gets in his way. The days of Chambliss and Kewan Lacy backfields are over this year, and the former will need to remind the Rebels' faithful of the leader he is capable of being. Behind a reworked offensive line, I expect Chambliss to erase the doubts that have been growing surrounding him recently, and #6 will lead Ole Miss to victory in Norman on the heels of a strong offensive showing. Shekai Mills-Knight has the Best Rushing Performance of the Season While Lacy's legacy in Oxford looks like it will end full of questions about injuries and unfulfilled potential, the Rebels have a tailback capable of reshaping the team's rushing narrative late in the season. I wholeheartedly believe in Ole Miss' French-Canadian sophomore, and John David Baker's offensive scheming needs to rely on the talent that can line up beside Chambliss. Shekai Mills-Knight, when utilized by Baker, has been a revelation for Ole Miss' rushing attack; the only issue is that Knight has been used nowhere near enough. Makhi Frazier has left a lot to be desired since arriving at Ole Miss from Michigan State, and with Knight receiving the leftover touches, the Rebels have seen what the sophomore back is capable of. If Shekai Mills-Knight is given an uptick in touches in Norman, there is no reason that the tailback cannot eclipse Ole Miss' single-game leading rusher this season: Kewan Lacy's 122-yard showing against Missouri. The Rebels need to be more dynamic offensively, and it all starts with feeding the Canadian native. The Defense Holds Oklahoma Under 21 Georgia's offense was able to do whatever it wanted in Oxford last weekend, and the Rebels will need to suffocate John Mateer and the Sooners under the new Jason Witten-led offense. Ole Miss has lived off of its offense for the past two seasons, and with how things have gone recently, a strong defensive showing in Norman will go a long way, not just towards a win but towards proving to the selection committee that the Rebels are worthy of making the postseason. Golding's defense has the talent to be great, now it just needs to translate to the field. Kickoff is set for 4:15 p.m. EST on SEC Network. Ole Miss is favored by 1.5 points on the spread with a moneyline of -104. The total is set at 49.5 points. Here's my Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 14, 2026. Ole Miss vs. Oklahoma Pick: Oklahoma -1 or Better My Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss best bet is on the Sooners. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page . Ole Miss vs Oklahoma Odds Ole Miss vs Oklahoma point spread : Ole Miss -1.5 (+110), Oklahoma +1.5 (-130) Ole Miss vs Oklahoma over/under : 49.5 (-110o / -110u) Ole Miss vs Oklahoma moneyline : Ole Miss -104, Oklahoma -115 I couldn't have been more wrong about last week's playoff rematch between Ole Miss and Georgia. The Rebels got absolutely stomped from start to finish in every facet. Now, with three losses under their belts and only games against Mississippi State and Wofford remaining over the final two weeks, I don't see a path to the College Football Playoff, which the Ole Miss locker room is likely fully aware of. There's a reason you're hearing about season-ending injuries and the portal already in Oxford. Do they show up this week in Norman? It's certainly a question worth posing for a team that had national title aspirations. Even if Ole Miss is fully locked in during practice all week and shows up ready to roll on Saturday, I still would feel confident holding a Sooners ticket. Let's start with injuries, where these two teams are headed in opposite directions. The Rebels recently learned star running back Kewan Lacy will shut it down for the remainder of the season. Plus, they will have to make do this week without their best offensive lineman in Patrick Kutas and leading tackler in linebacker Keaton Thomas. Meanwhile, the Oklahoma offensive line is finally getting back to full strength. The biggest addition was getting starting left tackle Michael Fasusi back a few weeks ago. There was previously a massive void at left tackle, which has since been filled by the former five-star who finally looked 100% healthy last week at Florida. Not only will pass protection improve immensely, but the running game should continue to look more competent the rest of the season, especially against an Ole Miss defense that has plenty of holes against the run and pass. Last week also marked the debut of Oklahoma's new play-caller, Jason Witten. I thought he did a fantastic job with play sequencing, and the entire operation just looked cleaner. Most importantly, Oklahoma didn't have any turnovers, which have absolutely killed them all season. Witten also unleashed John Mateer with a higher rate of designed runs. It also helps that Mateer is finally playing with confidence. Earlier in the season, he could barely scramble without literally dropping the ball and was extremely hesitant to fire on his reads. It was as if he almost had the quarterback version of the yips. With that said, it's not like this offense is going to turn into the 1999 Rams. This is still a team that's led by an elite defense that should get constant pressure on Trinidad Chambliss, especially without Kutas and a backfield that struggles in picking up blitzes. Chambliss has really struggled against the last two top-tier defenses he faced in Texas and Georgia. This is just not the same offense as last year. Not only is Lacy done for the year, but there's a new play-caller, and the pass-catchers aren't as talented. As a result, Chambliss' efficiency numbers have fallen precipitously when under pressure. That could spell doom against a Brent Venables stop unit that generates pressure at one of the highest rates in the country. From a regression standpoint, don't be surprised if Oklahoma falls on a key fumble or two. The Sooners have the lowest fumble recovery rate in the country at 23%, while the Rebels rank 20th in that department at nearly 80%. This is not my typical buy-low / sell-high spot, as Ole Miss got blown out last week, while Oklahoma pulled off a road upset. However, I still think this sets up well for the Sooners, who are trending up offensively with a defense that should give Chambliss fits. And I do question whether or not we get a fully locked-in Rebels bunch this week. Pick: Oklahoma -1 or Better

picks.headline: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line
picks.blurb: 5 Ole Miss vs Oklahoma predictions with Trinidad Chambliss, Rebels' CFP chances on line - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Sam Hutchens, Mississippi Clarion Ledger · The Clarion Ledger Thu, November 12, 2026 at 11:03 AM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads OXFORD − Ole Miss football must win on the road against Oklahoma to keep hopes of a College Football Playoff appearance alive. No. 17 Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) will play at Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3) on Nov. 14 (3:15 p.m., SEC Network). The Rebels are coming off a 42-7 home loss to No. 1 Georgia that put its CFP hopes on the edge of extinction. A viable path to the CFP begins with winning the final three games of the season. This is the third consecutive season Ole Miss has faced Oklahoma and the Rebels have won the first two matchups. Like Ole Miss, the Sooners made the College Football Playoff in 2025. OU returned quarterback John Mateer but has struggled to complement a strong defense with a steady offense. Although the Sooners have losses to Michigan, No. 1 Georgia, No. 13 Kentucky and No. 24 South Carolina, OU has beaten two teams that Ole Miss lost to in No. 8 Texas and Florida. Here are five predictions about the matchup, including the final score: Jason Witten will have new wrinkles for OU offense vs Ole Miss defense The matchup pits defensive coaches against each other in Ole Miss' Pete Golding and OU's Brent Venables. Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten could be the wild card. The former Dallas Cowboys tight end was elevated to the interim offensive coordinator position after Oklahoma fired Ben Arbuckle. Five days after Arbuckle was dismissed, OU beat Florida 23-7 in a game where it had 351 total yards. The Oklahoma offense played clean, efficient football under Witten. The Sooners suddenly seem to have new life offensively, which comes at a bad time for an Ole Miss defense that was ravaged for 481 yards vs Georgia. Trinidad Chambliss, John Mateer both throw interceptions With three games remaining, Chambliss' interceptions have tripled this season. He threw three in a spectacular 2025 season, but is up to nine in 2026. Golding attributed the increase to a combination of bad reads, bad luck and bad throws. Chambliss has thrown at least one interception in seven games this season. That plays into the hands of Oklahoma, which is No. 4 in the SEC with nine interceptions. The Sooners are also No. 5 in the conference with 26 sacks. Chambliss has been more vulnerable when under pressure. OU quarterback John Mateer has had turnover problems as well. He's thrown seven interceptions and has two lost fumbles. Look for both defenses to come up with an interception. The Sooners' stingy defense is better prepared to recover from interceptions than Ole Miss. When OU picks off Chambliss, it will give the ball back to a Sooners' offense that looks well prepared to chew clock and limit the chances for the Rebels' offense. Ole Miss gives Makhi Frazier, Shekai Mills-Knight both at least 10 carries Even with a quarterback as capable as Chambliss, it will be hard for Ole Miss to attack Oklahoma through the air. OU has the No. 1 passing defense in the SEC (170.7 yards per game). OU is No. 7 in the SEC in rushing defense (122.6 yards per game), but it's the weaker of two stout options. Ole Miss needs running backs Shekai Mills-Knight and Makhi Frazier to play well. Those two players are the primary backs with Kewan Lacy ruled out with a shoulder injury. Mills-Knight and Frazier combined for 17 carries for 60 yards vs Georgia, but they should get more carries against Oklahoma. Oklahoma leads in time of possession, Ole Miss relies on big plays Opponents are 31-for-112 (27.7%) on third down conversions against the Sooners. That's the lowest mark in the SEC and No. 4 nationally. That indicates Ole Miss will have trouble maintaining long, slow-developing drives. The key to combat that is explosive plays. Ole Miss could use a big game from Deuce Alexander. The receiver leads Ole Miss with 669 receiving yards, but he was held without a catch against Georgia. He is Ole Miss' fastest, most explosive player and the primary threat to score a deep touchdown. Ole Miss is on the other end of the spectrum. The Rebels allow 44% of third down conversions, which is No. 14 in the SEC. The Sooners clinched the game against Florida with a 20-play march in the fourth quarter that consumed 12:45 on the clock. The Rebels must avoid that fate. Ole Miss vs Oklahoma score prediction Oklahoma 24, Ole Miss 23: This should be a close game that will be determined by whether Ole Miss' defense or Oklahoma's offense does better. Right now it feels like the OU offense has more momentum. The Rebels are more desperate, but feeling like you need to press and make big plays on the road against OU's defense is a bad place to be. The Rebels currently have a 17% chance to make it . With a win on Saturday, that jumps to 28%. Of course, the Sooners don't really have a chance anymore . But they can still play the spoiler role. This new-look offense under Jason Witten could surprise Ole Miss. The Rebels should find more success with explosive plays, and Chambliss looks much more comfortable running the offense. Oklahoma's defense will have its moments, especially as the game progresses, but I think Ole Miss will score early enough to put points on the board and establish control. Oklahoma has been disappointing on offense this year, though the change at OC seems to have reinvigorated that unit. The Rebels are holding on for dear life in their playoff hopes, and it all starts with Trinidad Chambliss on offense. picks.blurb: Sooners Wire Staff predictions for Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Sooners Wire Staff predictions for Oklahoma vs. Ole Miss Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Oklahoma Sooners (5-4, 3-3 SEC) and the Ole Miss Rebels (6-3, 4-3 SEC ) meet for the third straight season and the second consecutive season in Norman. Oklahoma is 0-3 all-time in the series but is coming off of one of its most complete games of the season in their win over the Florida Gators . The offense found a rhythm and consistency we haven't seen much this year, and the defense suffocated the Florida Gators, holding them to seven points and forcing two interceptions. This week, with the Rebels coming to town, the Sooners face a much different challenge. Ole Miss boasts one of the most dynamic quarterbacks in college football, in Trinidad Chambliss. Chambliss is 15th in the nation in passing yards and second in the SEC behind LSU's Sam Leavitt. He's a threat to make plays with his legs as well, as we saw last year in the Rebels' win in Norman. On a slippery Owen Field, Chambliss threw for 315 yards and ran for 53 yards in Ole Miss's 34-26 win over Oklahoma. The Sooners defense will need to do a better job containing Chambliss if they want to win this Saturday and earn bowl eligibility. Can Oklahoma find a way to earn back-to-back victories for the first time since the LSU and Missouri wins at the end of last season? Here's how our staff at Sooners Wire sees the game playing out. Sooners Defense Leads to Win Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Oklahoma Sooners defensive back Peyton Bowen (22) runs to score a touchdown against the Texas Longhorns during the second half at Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images It'll be a battle between two defense-minded coaches, and the Sooners are still riding high with Interim offensive coordinator Jason Witten at the helm, while Ole Miss' offense is sputtering thanks to key injuries to its offensive line, star running back, and possibly the quarterback. For one of the few times this season, the injury report looks to be in favor of Oklahoma, which is looking to build on a win for the first time this season. With everyone theoretically healthy, one of the advantages Oklahoma has is that Ole Miss QB Trinidad Chambliss has become turnover-prone, throwing nine interceptions this season, while OU's defense does well at forcing those turnovers, coming in at No. 4 in the conference. It's no secret that the Sooners are typically successful when they win the turnover battle, and I think that will play a role in this one. It'll be a defensive battle, but OU will have the edge at home. Oklahoma 17, Ole Miss 14 James D. Jackson, Contributor Ole Miss Responds This season, Oklahoma has typically followed up an encouraging step forward with a discouraging step back, ever since the Texas game. Ole Miss is reeling after last week's loss to Georgia, and Brent Venables typically doesn't have his team as on point when the opponent is more desperate and hungry than the Sooners are. Things will probably slip after last week's upset win; there's too much of a pattern to think otherwise. If Trinidad Chambliss plays like he's capable of, Ole Miss wins. If OU recaptures some of the magic of last November, when the Sooners played consistent football, they can put an end to Ole Miss' teetering playoff hopes. Ole Miss 20, Oklahoma 17 Aaron Gelvin, Contributor Ole Miss has the Better QB Oct 31, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) drops back to pass during the fourth quarter against the Auburn Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images The Oklahoma Sooners continued their uneven play this season with a win over the Florida Gators. The Sooners have yet to win or lose back-to-back games this season. While it looked much better offensively under Jason Witten, the question is whether that will continue against the Ole Miss Rebels. This game is a true toss-up, but I've got to go with the quarterback I trust more and that's Trinidad Chambliss. Ole Miss 24, Oklahoma 17 Jaron Spor, Contributor Offense Does it Again Nov 7, 2026; Gainesville, Florida, USA; Oklahoma Sooners quarterback John Mateer (10) throws the ball during the first half against the Florida Gators at Ben Hill Griffin Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Pendleton-Imagn Images The Oklahoma offense took a positive step in the right direction last week with their road win over Florida. They found a way to win with a ball-control style that helped the Sooners win the time-of-possession battle by 15 minutes. The Sooners scored on three of their first four drives, laying the groundwork for what could be the plan to keep Trinidad Chambliss and the Rebels' offense at bay this weekend. Ole Miss allows 394.7 yards per game, which is 15th in the SEC and 104th in the nation. This could be another opportunity for the Sooners' offense to take a big step forward. Ole Miss won 34-26. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Tyler Komis · Ole Miss Rebels On SI Fri, November 13, 2026 at 12:30 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Ole Miss is looking to regroup in Norman against Oklahoma and needs to win out in order to possibly contend for a spot in the College Football Playoffs. The Rebels fell nine spots in this week's CFP rankings, following its uncompetitive loss to Georgia, and no longer possess control of their postseason destiny. Ole Miss On SI's Tyler Komis and co-host Bailey Flanders dive into Ole Miss' season up to this point and preview its game against Oklahoma this weekend. The two also discuss how realistic the program's path back to the CFP is this season in episode 111 of The Rebel Rundown . What Golding said about Oklahoma Oct 17, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels head coach Pete Golding looks on before the game against the Missouri Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect "I think the defensive concepts of both defensive head coaches as well - it's like, 'okay, how do I shrink the game, number one, when you're playing an explosive offense?' That's by controlling the football, being able to establish the run game, which both those guys believe in. I think being defensive guys, you know what creates issues on defense alternative formations," Golding said. "I think you saw that with Florida. Last week there's ten snaps of unbalance plus one run game. I think they're getting the quarterback going in the run game as well to make you account for all 11. And then from a defensive standpoint create negative yardage plays (and are) very aggressive. Venables' defense is very much like you saw on Saturday (against Georgia). You know that was probably one of their higher pressure games being Georgia. You know a lot of seven up looks and things like that." "I think some of the post-snap RPO game has been eliminated a little bit. Some of that decision making process for the quarterback. They still have RPOs. I think a lot of them are pre-snap box generated based on numbers and free access and things like that. I think a lot of the run schemes are similar in the same way. I think they're trying to get the quarterback's legs going a little more than before. They've always had some quarterback designed runs, but it felt like that was more of an emphasis in the Florida game. Obviously (Jason) Witten being a tight end, the tight end's going to be a piece of the package, and they've got some good tight ends," Golding said of Oklahoma's new interim offensive coordinator. "You know 81 is a really good player. But I think taking more off the quarterback you know as far as from a progression standpoint and reads post-snap and being a little more specific in the run game based on formation. A little more alternative with a shift and a motion, which has kind of been the theme against us anyway. So I think simplifying it within reason and then making you account for the quarterback." The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. More news : Brian Kelly Sends Blunt Warning to Texas Ahead of LSU Clash Lacy quickly emerged as one of the best players in college football last season, rushing for 1,567 yards (third most in FBS) and 24 touchdowns (second) on an FBS-leading 306 attempts, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, along with 177 receiving yards. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. His third, and potentially final, college season ends after just six games, finishing with 388 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 78 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Makhi Frazier, a Junior transfer from Michigan State, and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight will continue to handle the bulk of the carries for Ole Miss. Frazier has 365 rushing yards on 72 carries this season (5.1 yards per carry), while Mills-Knight has 165 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. The Ole Miss Rebels are 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play after their brutal 42-7 loss to Georgia last weekend in Oxford. Two weeks before that, they fell 34-27 at Texas. Those are two ranked opponents who are firmly in the College Football Playoff Conversation, but it's too late in the season to be dropping games like that. Now they head into a crucial SEC clash at Oklahoma on Saturday, with the CFP potentially hanging in the balance. More news : Brian Kelly Sends Blunt Warning to Texas Ahead of LSU Clash Lacy quickly emerged as one of the best players in college football last season, rushing for 1,567 yards (third most in FBS) and 24 touchdowns (second) on an FBS-leading 306 attempts, averaging 5.1 yards per carry, along with 177 receiving yards. He earned first-team All-American and first-team All-SEC honors, and entered this year on the preseason watchlist for several national awards. But Lacy injured his left shoulder in the Rebels' loss to Texas on Oct. 24, and hasn't been able to recover. His third, and potentially final, college season ends after just six games, finishing with 388 rushing yards and five rushing touchdowns on 78 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Makhi Frazier, a Junior transfer from Michigan State, and sophomore Shekai Mills-Knight will continue to handle the bulk of the carries for Ole Miss. Frazier has 365 rushing yards on 72 carries this season (5.1 yards per carry), while Mills-Knight has 165 yards and three touchdowns on 33 carries (5.0 yards per carry). Ole Miss coach Pete Golding confirmed his squad will be without two of its most important offensive players when the Rebels line up against the Sooners. Golding said running back Kewan Lacy and starting offensive lineman Patrick Kutas will miss the game. So far this season, the Sooners have typically had the least desirable injury report. But the two losses for Ole Miss are fairly significant, especially given the Rebels are coming off their third loss of the season. Golding said Kutas was injured in Ole Miss’ 42-7 loss at Georgia on Nov. 7. The Rebels will have to make adjustments across the offensive line. Former Sooner Troy Everett will likely replace Kutas at right guard as he did against Georgia. “Not season-ending,” Golding said of Kutas’ injury in his weekly presser. “Kutas got banged up pretty good, so we will not have Patrick this week. So there will be some moving parts to that and looking at some guys bumping inside. Golding later clarified Lacy will not play either. Against the Sooners last season, Lacy rushed 27 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns to help No. 8 Ole Miss defeat No. 13 Oklahoma 34–26. This season, however, he has missed a handful of games due to injury. Lacy missed the Georgia game, and it was a noticeable absence. Ole Miss (6-3, 4-3 SEC) mustered only 7 points against the Bulldogs. Lacy was a Doak Walker Award finalist last season. The honor is presented annually to the nation's top college football running back. He has run for five touchdowns this season but hasn’t seen the field since dislocating his shoulder against Texas in October. Ole Miss has lost two of the last three games in his absence. Oklahoma (5-4, 3-3 SEC) will have an opportunity to take advantage in Norman with kickoff scheduled for 3:15 p.m. CT. The game will be televised on the SEC Network. This is the third straight season the Sooners have played the Rebels and second straight season Oklahoma has hosted them. The league named the two schools annual rivals last season, meaning they'll play each other at home every season for at least the next four years. Ole Miss is 3-0 against the Sooners, who are trying to build on a 23-7 win over Florida . A win would also keep Oklahoma's bowl streak alive. home.blurb: Ole Miss listed Chambliss as probable for Saturday in the initial SEC availability report , putting the Rebels' starting quarterback on track to play. However, the Rebels didn't detail the injury, and Chambliss didn't show issues in last weekend's game. That makes Chambliss' probable designation significant for an Ole Miss team attempting to recover from its worst offensive performance of the season. The Rebels managed only seven points in Saturday's 42-7 loss to Georgia, falling to 6-3 overall and 4-3 in SEC play. Who will win Florida vs Kentucky today: Kentucky -3.5 After a hot September that had Florida ranked in the top 10 and climbing the college football national championship odds , the Gators have been one of the worst teams in the SEC. Since upsetting Ole Miss, Florida is 1-4 straight-up and against the spread, and its struggles will continue against Jon Sumrall's alma mater. I would take Kentucky to cover up to -4.5 . Florida is coming off its worst loss of the season, losing 23-17 at home to Oklahoma as a 3.5-point favorite, and switching back to Aaron Philo at QB won't save a team that's averaging 15.6 points per game since the start of October. The last time we saw Philo, he was benched in the World's Largest Outdoor Cocktail Party. Kentucky's defense isn't Georgia's, but it is disruptive enough to slow Florida down. The Wildcats rank 21st nationally in havoc rate (18.9%) and seventh in interceptions (12). See our college football picks against the spread for more Week 11 sides. Kentucky's offense is far more efficient, and the reason I'd play the Over at 52.5 or better . The Wildcats have one of the best offensive lines in the country, paving the way for a unit ranked 16th nationally in success rate (49.2%) . With Kenny Minchey's efficiency (77.8% adjusted completion percentage) and the Wildcats' advantage on the line, they shouldn't have trouble converting on money downs against a defense sitting 132nd in third/fourth down success rate (54.8%). However, the Gators will move the ball too against a Kentucky defense that struggles to stop the run. The Wildcats are currently 96th in defensive success rate (45.8%), and Florida running back Jadan Baugh ranks top 10 nationally in forced missed tackles (48).
