The Kentucky Wildcats look to bounce back from last week's brutal loss at Tennessee when they host the rival Florida Gators on Saturday night. My Florida vs Kentucky prop picks feature two Wildcats who should thrive against the Gators' struggling defense, plus a Florida quarterback who could benefit from a pass-heavy game script. For more college football picks and analysis, check out Rob Paul's Florida vs Kentucky predictions ahead of kickoff at 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Best Florida vs Kentucky props Prop pick #1: CJ Baxter Over 63.5 rushing yards Kentucky's offense has rolled when it hasn't faced a high-caliber defense this season, and Florida certainly doesn't qualify. I'm backing CJ Baxter to have himself a day, and I'd play this rushing total up to 56% against a Florida front that ranks among the nation's worst in stuff rate . The Gators rank in the bottom half nationally in explosive run rate allowed, a key reason they're 93rd in EPA per rush and 111th in success rate. The Wildcats rank third in success rate this year and sit in the 83rd percentile in explosive run rate. Baxter's 38.8% breakaway yard rate ranks 29th among 116 backs with at least 90 carries. With a game script that should see him get 15-plus carries, this one's a no-brainer for me. Prop pick #2: Willie Rodriguez Over 48.5 receiving yards Florida's defense allowed Oklahoma tight end Rocky Beers to rack up 72 yards on just four catches last week, his best game since September. That's why I'm backing Willie Rodriguez for a strong outing, playable up to 55%. Rodriguez ranks second on the Wildcats in targets. In Will Stein's offense, quarterback Kenny Minchey has been taught to take what's given to him, and the tight end has become a reliable option. Brad White's soft zone defense ranks 120th in defensive passing success rate and sits in the 18th percentile in explosive pass rate. Rodriguez ranks sixth among all tight ends in yards after catch (YAC). He's caught at least five passes in six of Kentucky's seven SEC games, and that consistent volume makes this receiving total very attainable. Prop pick #3: Aaron Philo Over 194.5 passing yards Sources have confirmed that Aaron Philo will start at quarterback for Florida this week, and I'm backing him to clear this total, playable up to 54%. I don't think Philo will have a good game overall, as the Wildcats should get after him and pick him off at least once. But this Kentucky defense is prone to giving up big plays through the air and struggles to get off the field on third down, ranking 132nd in yards to gain and 115th in success rate. The Gators rank 29th in passing success rate , and they're often forced into passing situations because of the ridiculous number of penalties committed by their offensive line. Philo surpassed this number in all six of his starts before the Georgia game. With Kentucky expected to play from ahead, Philo should have enough passing opportunities to do so again, provided Jon Sumrall doesn't pull him. Greg Liodice · Action Network Sat, November 14, 2026 at 6:05 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Florida Gators take on the Kentucky Wildcats in Lexington, Kentucky, on Saturday, Nov. 14. Kickoff is set for 6:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. Kentucky is favored by 2.5 points (-110) on the spread with a moneyline of -156. Florida enters as a 2.5-point (-110) underdog and is +130 on the moneyline to pull off the upset. The over/under sits at 52.5 total points (-115o / -105u). Here's my Florida vs. Kentucky prediction and college football pick for Saturday, November 14. Florida vs. Kentucky Pick: Kentucky -3.5 My Kentucky vs. Florida best bet is on the Wildcats to cover the spread. Find the best line available on our live NCAAF odds page and make sure to download the Action Network app for more picks and analysis. Florida vs Kentucky Odds, Betting Lines & Over/Under Florida vs Kentucky point spread : Kentucky -2.5 (-110), Florida +2.5 (-110) Florida vs Kentucky over/under : 52.5 (-115o / -105u) Florida vs Kentucky moneyline : Florida +130, Kentucky -156 Has any program this season had a worse breakdown than Florida? It seemed like the Gators were expediting their rebuild after pulverizing Ole Miss, 52-28, in Week 4, but that couldn't be further from the truth. Since that very game, Florida has gone 1-4 and has scored a total of just 15 points in its past two games. Further to that point, head coach Jon Sumrall can't seem to figure out what quarterback he wants to start. Last week against Oklahoma , Tramell Jones Jr. started. This week? It's back to Aaron Philo, who truly wasn't the problem. He had that one insanely embarrassing interception against Georgia , but there's no reason he should've been punished for that. I like Sumrall a lot as a coach, but the benching of Philo was awfully reactionary. If you think about it, the passing game has been one of the better parts of this offense. Running back Jadan Baugh has gone invisible since one of the hottest stretches for a running back, where he ran for 135 yards in four consecutive games. Since then, Baugh has averaged 3.1 yards per carry. What happened? The offensive line is what happened. In the first four games, Philo was only sacked twice. In this five-game stretch, Florida's quarterbacks were sacked 14 times. Defensively, this hasn't been a team to write home about either. The Gators are just OK at stopping the run, allowing 143.8 rushing yards per game, but the secondary has been brutal. DJ Coleman and Cormani McClain have been decent, but this unit allows way too many yards through the air, ranking 102nd with 243.1 passing yards allowed. Kentucky has been one of the biggest surprises this season, and it's all because of head coach Will Stein, who has changed the complete landscape of this program. It will be interesting to see how Kentucky's defense handles Florida's struggling offense. The Wildcats have their moments, and their moments are strong, generating Havoc at an 18.3% clip (27th). Defensive backs Ty Bryant and Jordan Castell each have four interceptions, while lineman Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace has been a dog on the front lines with six sacks and three PBUs. The problem is, they're susceptible to explosive plays, especially on the ground, ranking 81st in explosiveness allowed and 109th in rushing Success Rate allowed. Quarterback Kenny Minchey has been exceptional this season after spending three seasons at Notre Dame . Minchey has only turned the ball over twice and has completed passes at a 70% clip. Not only that, the offensive line has done a solid job at protecting him, allowing Havoc on just 18.3% of snaps. He's developed a nice chemistry with a nice chemistry with Kenny Darby and tight end Willie Rodriguez, who each have three receiving touchdowns. However, what's separated Kentucky from the pack has been its run game, ranking second in Success Rate. Both CJ Baxter and Jason Patterson each average over 5.5 yards per carry, with Baxter running it into the endzone eight times. Given how poorly Florida's defense has been, and how it can't seem to protect Philo, I see this being a long night for him. The name of the game is applying pressure to the quarterback, and when Florida lets up consistent pressure, it loses. Kentucky's defense isn't perfect, but the one thing it does right is shield its own weaknesses. Factor in that this game is being played in Lexington, and I like Kentucky to bounce back from getting trounced by Tennessee last week. Give me the Wildcats to cover. Pick: Kentucky -3.5

picks.headline: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction
picks.blurb: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NCAAF College Fantasy Football College Football Playoff College football live updates FAA ground stop updates SEC moves Ole Miss-OU to Sunday Colorado ends Houston's CFP hopes Story by Wildcats Wire Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction Braxton Howard, UK Wildcats Wire · Wildcats Wire Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:57 PM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Will Stein's Kentucky football team hosts Jon Sumrall's Florida Gators team under the lights at Kroger Field tomorrow at 6:15 P.M. ET. Florida has came back down to earth after a strong September and Kentucky is looking to bounce back after suffering their second loss of the season. We preview the Gators offense and defense, as well as laid out the path to victory for the Wildcats. Now, I will give my final thoughts on the matchup and a prediction for the game. Coach Stein said that last week was only the second time in his coaching career that his offense failed to score a touchdown. This team and the offense specifically will be looking to make a statement tomorrow night. They will get a perfect opportunity against a Brad White defense that has struggled all season for the Gators. As we know from watching years of Brad White's scheme in Lexington, they love to play soft zone coverage and allow easy completions to offenses in hopes of executing a bend-don't-break style of defense. The big advantage is this Kentucky offense is built off of efficiency and getting Kenny Minchey easy completions in quick game. This creates an advantageous scheme matchup for Will Stein and offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. If the Wildcats can eliminate the self-inflicted mistakes from last week in Knoxville, you have to like their chances to put together long scoring drives. The difference in this game being close and the Cats running away with it is if the offense can start to find the explosive plays. One area of this matchup we have not talked about is the weather aspect of this football game on Saturday. The past few days in Lexington have turned extremely cold, and temperatures for kickoff at looking at 40 degrees or below. Combine that with the winds, it will be freezing at Kroger Field and will only get colder as the game goes on. You have to wonder how this Florida team will respond in these conditions especially if they don't start fast in this one. This Florida team is reeling, they have lost four of their last five games. The drop-off has been eye-opening for the Gators because they looked like one of the best teams in the country through the first month of the season. Defenses have figured out how to bottle up their run game and the offense has started to suffer because of it. The Gators offense led them to their hot start to the Jon Sumrall era and covered up the rough play on the defensive side of the football. Kentucky has to stop this rushing attack and get Florida into a dropback heavy game. The Gators are going back to Aaron Philo after starting Tramell Jones last week. The old saying goes: if you have two quarterbacks, you have none. I think the Wildcats will be prepared to potentially see both guys this week as the Gators will try everything they can to generate some offense. Florida has to answer questions offensively, their offensive line is one of the worst in the conference and the quarterback situation is not ideal. Brad White has not figured out how to fix the Gators defensive issues in his first year away from Lexington. I think Kentucky capitalizes on that and has one of their best offensive performances of the season following last week where they failed to reach the end zone. Kentucky has their backs against the wall, they will make the College Football Playoff if they win the last three games and I believe the offense makes a statement in the cold at Kroger Field. Prediction: Kentucky 38, Florida 20 This article originally appeared on UK Wildcats Wire: Kentucky vs Florida: Final thoughts, prediction

away.headline: Gators Announce Starting QB Ahead of Clash with No. 11 Kentucky
away.blurb: GAINESVILLE, Fla. — The Florida Gators are making yet another change at quarterback. Aaron Philo, who had been benched for last week’s loss to Oklahoma , will return as the starter for this week’s game at Kentucky. CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz was first to report. The decision is the latest in a series of moves at the position between Philo and Tramell Jones Jr., as struggles at the position have mounted over the last month. Philo was replaced by Jones Jr. in losses to Missouri and South Carolina before missing the Texas game with an injury. Jones Jr. threw for two touchdowns in that start and replaced Philo after three drives, two weeks later in the loss to Georgia. Last week’s loss to the Sooners was a negative turning point for the true sophomore, though, with Jones Jr. completing just 10 of his 22 passes for 133 yards, no touchdowns, and two interceptions. He played all but one offensive snap, with Philo coming in for a handoff for just one play. “Think both guys have done some really good things this year at times, and both guys have done some not-so-good things at times,” head coach Jon Sumrall said on Monday. “Didn't think we played well enough at quarterback on Saturday.” Jones Jr. is also dealing with an undisclosed injury that Sumrall said could require surgery in the offseason. However, Jones Jr. said after the loss that the injury is not holding him back. Florida’s recent struggles at the position — a microcosm of other issues on the offensive line, injury issues at receiver, and difficulties in the run game with the running backs — have led to outside discussions on the long-term status of the position and both Philo’s and Jones Jr.’s individual futures with the program. Offensive coordinator Buster Faulkner said the team’s focus remains on developing those currently on the roster and not looking towards the NCAA Transfer Portal to address the position. “We got three games to evaluate everything,” he said. “Look, one thing about me is if I tell you, like, I do believe in them. And I do understand that it is a process with the quarterback position, and I will not rush that process, right? I want to stand by those guys. I'm gonna bring them along. It's our job to coach them.” Kickoff on Saturday between Florida and Kentucky is at 6:15 p.m., with television coverage on ESPN. Have the Florida Gators Reopened its Quarterback Battle? away.blurb: Wide receiver Lawayne McCoy is expected to return after nearly a month on the sidelines, giving quarterback Lincoln Kienholz another important option in the passing game. Louisville WR LaWayne McCoy will return today after nearly a month, sources tell @On3. The coach also indicated that he did not expect McCoy to return immediately. However, the wide receiver’s recovery has progressed, and he was listed as probable on the ACC availability report ahead of Saturday’s matchup. McCoy’s return could be particularly important for Louisville’s offensive production. He has averaged 20.5 yards per reception across seven appearances this season. His 513 receiving yards and four touchdowns have made him one of the Cardinals’ most productive offensive weapons. Louisville’s offense is set to receive a timely boost as the Cardinals prepare for their road matchup against North Carolina. On3 national reporter Pete Nakos shared the development on X , reporting that McCoy will be back in action on Saturday. Nakos also highlighted McCoy’s production this season. writing: “(McCoy) Has 25 catches for 513 yards and 4 TDs this season. Cardinals are at North Carolina.” McCoy last played against Syracuse on October 17. He caught five passes for 93 yards in Louisville’s 34-26 victory. Further testing revealed that the injury was more serious than initially believed. The wide receiver subsequently missed Louisville’s games against Stanford and Georgia Tech. Louisville head coach Jeff Brohm initially provided a cautious update about McCoy’s recovery ahead of the Stanford game on Oct. 31. Speaking about the injury, Brohm said : “I don’t think it requires surgery, but we have to get it healed. So the timetable is kind of unknown now.” Louisville enters Saturday’s contest with considerable momentum. The Cardinals defeated Georgia Tech 44-17 on Nov. 7, extending their winning streak to four games. They currently hold a 6-3 overall record and a 5-2 mark in ACC play. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect Transfer Portal 2027 Top Recruits 2027 Top Classes College Football Rankings The Wildcats will try to spoil the Utes' perfect season in a ranked battle Big 12 battle Getty Images Utah's trip to Arizona in Week 11 wasn't circled on many schedules before the 2026 college football season began, but the Big 12 matchup is a showdown between ranked teams and has serious College Football Playoff implications . The Utes are ranked No. 2 in the latest CFP poll as one of two undefeated teams remaining. After beating their hated rivals BYU last week, Utah's path to the Playoff -- and the Big 12 title game -- is clear, but they must turn the page quickly from taking down the Cougars as a trip to Tucson could prove tricky. Arizona climbed to No. 23 in this week's rankings after beating TCU in a thriller, and the 7-2 Wildcats' only losses this season have been to the other top teams in the Big 12 -- BYU and Texas Tech . Both of those losses came on the road, and Arizona will be relishing the opportunity to prove they belong in the top tier of the Big 12 when they finally get to welcome one of the big boys to southern Arizona. For the Utes, a win writes their name into the CFP bracket in pencil, as they'd improve to 10-0 with two games left where they'd be heavy favorites over TCU and West Virginia . The Wildcats, meanwhile, can pick up the biggest win of Brent Brennan's tenure and solidify their place in the Big 12's upper tier. The game was originally scheduled for the 7:30 p.m. ET primetime slot on Saturday, but due to travel issues caused by the FAA shutdown on Friday , kickoff was moved to 10:30 p.m. for this pivotal showdown. Utah vs. Arizona: Need to know Refocusing the Utes: The Utes put everything they had into winning The Holy War last week against BYU, in the first-ever matchup between the rivals while both were ranked in the top 10. It was obvious how much they put into the game plan with their hot start, and then they were forced to dig deep and rally after the Cougars answered with some haymakers of their own. That win was a proof point for Morgan Scalley in his first season as head coach, but this week might show us more about the kind of culture he's building in Salt Lake City. There's a natural urge to exhale after that kind of win, but Arizona is going to be juiced up for the chance to face the No. 2 team in the country at home. The Utes have to find a way to match that energy -- or at least withstand an early onslaught -- and get the game back on their terms. Strength on strength in the pass game: Arizona is one of the best passing offenses in the country with veteran quarterback Noah Fifita who is both efficient with a 73% completion rate and dynamic with 23 pass plays of 30-plus yards -- third-most in the country. Fifita and his favorite target Isaiah Mizell can take the lid off of most defenses and apply constant stress -- especially with Fifita's ability to extend plays and get outside the pocket. However, they'll be going up against one of the nation's best pass defenses that had Bear Bachmeier completely lost a week ago. Utah is allowing opposing quarterbacks to complete just 51.3% of passes (2nd lowest in the country) and is tied for fourth in interceptions with 13 (including four last week). The Utes pass defense is hyper aggressive, and they have four players with two or more interceptions this season. If there is one weakness to the Utah defense, it is that they have been susceptible to big plays in the passing game. The Utes have allowed 15 pass plays of 30+ yards this season, which ranks 104th in the country. Fifita and Arizona will have to take advantage of those opportunities for chunk plays when they present themselves because moving the ball consistently against the Utes is incredibly difficult. Arizona's pass rush vs. Devon Dampier : The Utes defense will get plenty of attention, but Arizona hasn't been a slouch on that side of the ball this year either. The strength of their defense is their pass rush, which is 10th in the nation in sacks per game (3.11). Devon Dampier is a tough quarterback to wrangle with his combination of strength and elusiveness, but the Wildcats are going to try to heat up Dampier to create some negative plays or, more ideally, turnovers. How Utah's offensive line handles Arizona's rush and how Dampier manages plays when the Wildcats do get pressure on him will be critical in this game. Utah has allowed just 13 sacks this season, thanks to a quality offensive line and Dampier's escapability, but that will be put to the test against the Wildcats. If Arizona is going to win this game, they need to find ways to get the Utes' offense behind the sticks and probably need to win the turnover battle. The Cougars made uncharacteristic mistakes all over the board, from four interceptions by Bear Bachmeier to 11 penalties and critical missed tackles. BYU actually outgained Utah by 6.1 to 5.3 yards per play, relying on special teams and turnovers to gain advantageous field position. Utah failed to establish a methodical drive on offense, finishing with nearly 10% fewer available yards than the national average. Quarterback Devon Dampier has filled the highlight reel this season, but a mark of 103rd in Havoc allowed has yet to translate to wins for the Utes. The Utah defense missed more tackles than BYU did in the game, sinking its PFF tackling grade further to 89th. The Utes continue to struggle to create a pass rush and have allowed explosive plays at critical moments. Utah's defense ranks 112th in passing downs EPA allowed, as head coach Morgan Scalley continues to see the undefeated defense fall outside the top 100 in 30-yard passes allowed. Arizona will have extra rest after a Friday night conference win over TCU . Although the Wildcats beat the Horned Frogs by a point, head coach Brent Brennan exited Week 10 with a 64% post-game win expectancy. Arizona averaged nearly two yards per play more than TCU , tossing eight explosive passes through the arm of quarterback Noah Fifita . The fifth-year senior has 21 passing touchdowns on the season with just six turnover-worthy plays, resulting in the lowest mistake rate of his career at Arizona. Fifita has two of the most dangerous weapons among any Power 4 pass-catching combinations: wideout Isaiah Mizell and slot receiver Giovanni Richardson. Richardson clocks in at 4.4 yards per route run, the only player in college football with 35 targets to exceed the explosiveness of Miami 's Malachi Toney . Danny Gonzales' nickel defense ranks highly in Success Rate but falls in the middle of FBS in generating Havoc . Arizona resides in the top 30 in Success Rate, closely matching a top-40 rank in yards per game and points allowed. The Wildcats have one of the lowest pressure rates this season but have made each attempt pay, ranking among the top 10 in sacks. Edge Chase Kennedy has six on the season, also tied in pressures with edge Cooper Blomstrom. One key to beating Utah will be average distance on third down, as Utah ranks fourth nationally in conversions, while Arizona is 77th in third-down defense. The Wildcats have at least a 51% Success Rate against all combinations and an even higher 60% Success Rate against zone read with two tight ends. Utah runs a heavy amount of outside zone with 12 personnel, an area Arizona should provide stops through the defensive line. When the Wildcats have the ball, Utah could struggle to defend Mizell and Richardson. The Utes have one of the heaviest man-coverage schemes in the FBS , but Fifita has carved up opponents in man coverage with a 51% Success Rate. A potential pivot to Cover 1 could increase the chances of an explosive play from Fifita, with an EPA of 0.25 per attempt. picks.blurb: Utah Utes expert previews the Arizona Wildcats football game, makes a score prediction | Arizona Desert Swarm Skip to main content SB Nation SB Nation logo An Arizona Wildcats Community Arizona Desert Swarm November 14, 2026 Arizona Desert Swarm Notifications Notifications The Feed Sections Arizona Basketball Arizona Football Arizona Softball Arizona Recruiting Arizona Soccer Arizona Volleyball Arizona Baseball Arizona Gymnastics Arizona in the Pros Betting Betting News FanDuel College Football Odds FanDuel College Basketball Odds Arizona Football Odds Arizona Basketball Odds College Football Picks and Predictions College Basketball Picks and Predictions Login / Sign Up Search The Feed Sections Expand Arizona Basketball Betting Expand Betting News Community Guidelines All communities Notifications Arizona Football During their decade-plus together in the Pac-12, Arizona and Utah had plenty of great battles, but the results tended to be streaky. The Wildcats won four straight meetings from 2012-15, then Utah took six in a row before the UA claimed the last two, including their Big 12 debut in 2024 when it beat a Top 10 Utes squad on the road. But the opponent coming to Tucson this weekend is better than any of those previous versions. Utah is 9-0 and ranked No. 2 nationally, one of two unbeaten teams in FBS. To better understand the Utes, we reached out to Josh Furlong of KSL.com for some insight and a score prediction. Below are his spirited answers to our lifeless questions: AZ Desert Swarm: What have been the main keys to Utah getting off to its best start since 2008? Josh Furlong: “The easy answer is quarterback Devon Dampier, who has been healthy and efficient as the team’s biggest playmaker, but it ultimately comes down to the culture Morgan Scalley has built at Utah in such a short time. He’s allowing the players to be loose while focused, understanding that it takes each person to contribute to wins. He’s an extremely competitive coach, but he’s able to pair that with a system that allows players to make mistakes, grow and develop.” Arizona fans still have nightmares about Devon Dampier from two years ago at New Mexico, and he seems to have only gotten better. Where has his game most improved this season, and is there anything he still struggles with? “Dampier has worked on going through his progressions and staying in the pocket more, which has allowed Utah to do more with him at QB. It’s giving him more structure while understanding that he still needs room to freelance and be the dynamic QB he can be. All of that has allowed him to have more confidence, especially now that he’s been paired with a better group of wide receivers. At times, though, he gets happy feet and doesn’t have the right mechanics in his throws, which can sometimes limit his passing.” Wayshawn Parker apparently got banged up against BYU but should be good to go for this game. What does he bring to the offense when healthy? “Wayshawn Parker simply opens up the options for Utah’s offense. His threat as a runner, especially as he breaks through tackles, makes him one of the top offensive names you have to take away. But by doing so, opposing defenses have to handle many other players that can be just as effective in advancing the offense — Dampier, Daniel Bray, Byrd Ficklin, Braden Pegan, Creed Whittemore, etc. On top of that, he’s really developed a great pass blocking game, which has been a huge advantage in keeping Dampier upright and doing what he does.” Arizona’s secondary has been dealing with injuries and got exploited a bit last week with deep passes. Who would be the beneficiaries of this in the Ute receiving corps? “The primary receiving target would be Braden Pegan (WR1), who is a multi-faceted receiver who can do pretty much anything needed, and is paired with Ricky Johnson and Creed Whittemore. Johnson is a smooth runner with great separation and great hands. Whittemore works primarily in the slot and has been great in the intermediate game, especially with opposing defenses focusing on Pegan and the potential run threats of Dampier, Ficklin, Parker. Another option is tight end Noah Bennee, who is the benefactor of all the other skills players being the top of mind. As the defense focuses on other players, Bennee sneaks out and can be a problem with his size.” How do you expect Utah to defend Arizona’s passing attack? “Utah will primarily operate in man coverage and force Noah Fifita to beat them one-on-one, while the defensive coordinator Colton Swan schemes up disguises and blitzes to keep Fifita uncomfortable. Because Fifita is so explosive, it’s likely Utah will try more contain while pressuring him.” Morgan Scalley had been the coach in waiting at Utah for a while, and we’re seeing why with this 9-0 start. What are the biggest differences between him and Kyle Whittingham? “The biggest difference is that Scalley is a people’s person. Kyle Whittingham cared more about coaching football and not the other elements, whereas Scalley sees it all interconnected. He shares the same hard-nosed, physical approach of Whittingham but wants a connected team that has no factions. It’s not, offense gets to know offense and defense gets to know defense, it’s a team-wide look as each works to understand the other. He’s also open to feedback, assuming that the feedback actually is presented in a way that helps change and it’s just complaining, though he’d listen to anyone who is frustrated. He wants all to feel connected and bought into the program, regardless of their standing with the team.” Prediction time. Does Utah move one step closer to an unbeaten regular season or does Arizona pull off a November upset at home and stay in the hunt for the Big 12 title game and the playoffs? Give us a score pick. “This game in Tucson is always a tricky one. Even when Utah has been the clear favorite, it’s far from a decisive win for the Utes. I think Scalley has his squad more focused on this game than it might have been in year’s past, which leads me to believe Utah will be ready for any blow and not be caught off guard in a road environment. I think Utah is the more complete team, but they’ve got to stop Fifita. To me, Utah wins this game if they can contain Fifita (as much as possible) and cannot give up momentum to an opposing crowd. I see Utah winning something like 31-24 .” Download the new SB Nation app All of your communities in one place. picks.headline: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU
picks.blurb: Three Bold Predictions for Texas' Saturday Night Showdown Against LSU Skip to main content SI.COM LONGHORNS NEWS 2025 Football Bracket FOOTBALL FOOTBALL FOOTBALL NEWS 2023 FOOTBALL COMMITS SI.COM LONGHORNS FB BASKETBALL NEWS SI.COM LONGHORNS BB The trouble with bold predictions is they tend to sound a little ridiculous — right up until they happen. There are plenty of reasonable expectations for Saturday night’s matchup between Texas and LSU. But reasonable expectations aren’t all that interesting, are they? So let’s throw a little caution to the wind. Maybe these predictions will look brilliant by the final whistle. Maybe they’ll be aging poorly before halftime. But that’s half the fun in the first place. Here are three bold predictions for the Longhorns’ trip to Baton Rouge. Raleek Brown Rushes for Over 100 Yards Nov 7, 2026; Columbia, Missouri, USA; Texas Longhorns running back Raleek Brown runs the ball during the first half against the Missouri Tigers at Faurot Field at Memorial Stadium. William Purnell-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. On paper, this might be the boldest prediction of the three. LSU enters Saturday allowing just 84.7 rushing yards per game, the second-best mark in the SEC. Meanwhile Texas has struggled to establish consistency on the ground for much of the season. But if there’s a Longhorn capable of bucking that trend, it’s Raleek Brown. Against Ole Miss, Brown demonstrated what an elite Texas run game could look like given the opportunity, carrying the ball 23 times for 157 yards. Last weekend, he once again flashed that potential, rushing for 85 yards on 17 attempts. With Sarkisian emphasizing the importance of avoiding situations where Texas falls behind the chains, establishing the run game early will likely be a priority. That could mean a concerted effort to feed Brown from the opening drive, allowing him to find his rhythm. It certainly won't be easy against an LSU defensive front that has made life miserable for opposing running backs all season. But if Sarkisian can get Brown going, don't be surprised if he eclipses the century mark. Colin Simmons Records Three Sacks Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns defensive end Colin Simmons in action during the game against the Oklahoma Sooners at the Cotton Bowl. Before his ankle injury, it would’ve been fair to argue that Colin Simmons was the best defensive player in the nation. Through his first six games, the junior accumulated 10.5 sacks — a metric he still leads the SEC in despite missing more than 2 games — and 16 tackles for loss. After playing just 18 snaps against Missouri, Simmons has yet to fully establish himself as the disruptive force that terrorized opposing offenses earlier in the season. Saturday might change that. LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt was sacked four times against Alabama last weekend, and Texas’ defensive front will prove to be another difficult assignment. But perhaps the most intriguing aspect of this prediction is Leavitt’s style of play. Leavitt has demonstrated a willingness to escape the pocket and improvise when plays begin to break down, often extending plays with his legs in hopes of creating something out of nothing. And while that ability makes him a dangerous dual-threat quarterback, it could also present an opportunity for a player with Simmons’ speed and relentless pursuit. Simmons doesn't necessarily need to beat his blocker immediately to disrupt a play. His closing speed allows him to pursue quarterbacks well after they've escaped the initial pressure, potentially turning Leavitt's improvisation into opportunities for sacks. Yes, three sacks is asking a lot, especially from a player still working his way back from an ankle injury. But if Simmons is even close to full strength, there's little reason to believe he can't once again take over a game. Texas Forces Three Turnovers Nov 7, 2026; Baton Rouge, Louisiana, USA; LSU Tigers quarterback Sam Leavitt looks to pass the ball during the second half against Alabama Crimson Tide at Tiger Stadium. Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Nine interceptions in nine games. Nine interceptions in nine games. That’s the rather alarming statistic surrounding Leavitt , even if those numbers don’t necessarily tell the full story. Not all nine interceptions have been his fault. But Leavitt has shown a tendency to misread defenders dropping into coverage and force throws into crowded windows, mistakes that Texas could be well-positioned to exploit. The Tigers have committed 13 turnovers this season, including four lost fumbles. And while Texas has forced just 10 turnovers through nine games, with Simmons healthy, Rasheem Biles playing some of his best football and a secondary capable of capitalizing on hurried throws, the Longhorns have all the pieces to give Texcalibur quite the night. He made his official prediction with CBS Sports this week. Kelly doesn't believe the Longhorns' offensive line will be up to the task of protecting quarterback Arch Manning against an elite LSU pass rush. "I've always felt that by the 10th week of the season, you are who you are. And I think those things will show with Texas and the inability to protect the quarterback. I worry about that," Kelly said about Texas's protection on CBS Sports airwaves . "For LSU, it's situational offense in particular. They were 0-for-4 on fourth down (against Alabama last week), and they were abysmal in the red zone. But I think you can fix those things, so I'm leaning toward LSU making the adjustments that they need to and winning the football game." Some fans might have expected Kelly to pick Texas for a few reasons. For starters, the Longhorns have a better collection of wins and are on a three-game winning streak. But on top of that, the narrative is that Kelly had some sort of grudge against LSU and will look to pick against them at every turn. However, Kelly's comments make it clear that he's confident in what LSU brings to the table in this matchup. home.blurb: Sophomore right tackle Weston Davis suffered a leg injury and did not return to the game. He was seen on crutches heading to the locker room after leaving the medical tent. Will the No. 22 LSU (6-3, 3-3 SEC) starting offensive line be back intact for the pivotal showdown against No. 8 Texas (7-2, 4-2) inside Tiger Stadium Saturday, Nov. 14? Davis was listed as "probable" on the Tigers' initial injury report released Wednesday, Nov. 11, for the matchup with the Longhorns . Defensive end Gabriel Reliford was listed as "probable" for the Tigers as well. Reliford tore his ACL in March and was initially thought to be out for the 2026 season. Star senior linebacker Whit Weeks was listed as "questionable." There were murmurs last week that Weeks could be cleared to play in time for the game against Alabama, but he was not able to come back from a fractured fibula last week. Questionable means he has a 50% chance to play against Texas this week. Safety Dashawn Spears, wide receiver Phillip Wright III, linebacker Charles Ross II and freshman defensive tackle Richard Anderson are all out for the game against Alabama. Davis, a redshirt sophomore, left the game after tight end Trey’Dez Green fell at his feet. The two-year starter couldn’t put any weight on his right leg as he was helped off the field and into the medical tent. He then hobbled to the locker room on crutches. LSU inserted Baylor transfer Sean Thompkins in Davis’ place at right tackle. Davis is a former four-star recruit who landed LSU’s starting right tackle job prior to the 2025 season. He and center Braelin Moore are the only holdover starters on the offensive line. Through eight games in 2026, Davis had allowed 21 pressures, according to Pro Football Focus data.
